Command-line companion for Kronikol. Includes `kronikol merge`, which combines several mergeable TestRunReport.json files (produced with GenerateMergeableData enabled — e.g. by parallel CI runners) into a single combined TestRunReport.html plus the merged TestRunReport.json beside it, so a sharded run is queryable and can serve as a baseline; `kronikol ingest`, which replays language-neutral NDJSON interaction captures (from an out-of-process proxy tap or any non-.NET capturer) into a full Kronikol report; `kronikol query`, which answers questions about a TestRunReport.json — why a test failed, what a service returned, where a wrong value came from — without loading the file, so a 10 MB report is debuggable by tooling and by AI agents; `kronikol export`, which pushes NDJSON interaction captures to an OTLP/HTTP collector as OpenTelemetry spans so the traffic only Kronikol saw appears in Tempo/Jaeger next to the app's real traces; `kronikol ctrf`, which converts a TestRunReport.json into a Common Test Report Format document so CI tooling that already speaks CTRF can read a Kronikol run; and `kronikol init-agents`, which installs the test-debugging skill and the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md instruction block into an existing repository, so its agents know the report is there and how to read it.

previous.description:
OctoNotes is a tool for generating release notes from Git repositories.

In a perfect, trunk-based world, there would be a single, linear graph between versions of an application. In the real world, however, that's almost never the case. Many releases will have hotfixes; many applications will have LTS branches or maintenance releases; not to mention pull requests and other reasons for branches, both short-lived and long.

OctoNotes takes a slightly different view of release notes. OctoNotes views the Git revision graph as the single source of truth. If a bug was fixed in a commit, that bug is only fixed in revisions containing that commit. If a feature was added between versions X and Y, it will appear in the Git revision graph as a commit somwehere between those two points.

By leveraging Git tags, OctoNotes can pinpoint precisely where in a Git revision graph a change was introduced, and provide the release notes for just the commits between two points on that graph.

By leveraging Git tags, OctoNotes can pinpoint precisely where in a Git revision graph a change was introduced, and provide the release notes for just the commits between two points on that graph.

Wraps Apple's accessibility audit and Google's Accessibility Test Framework, can capture what TalkBack says on Android, maps findings to WCAG 2.2 and labels the standards they are relevant to (Section 508, EN 301 549 and others), can point findings at a likely line in your own project (--source), and writes JSON, HTML, Markdown ticket, CSV, PDF and per-criterion evidence report output. It can also share a saved run as one file, signed by default. Automated checks find only some issues; manual testing is still required.
